title: Light level and duration of exposure determine the impact of self-luminous tablets on melatonin suppression
research_question: To investigate the impact of self-luminous tablet displays on nocturnal melatonin suppression, specifically how light level and duration of exposure from these devices affect melatonin levels.

participants.description: Mean age 18.9 ± 5.2 years (SD), young adults, non-smokers, no major health problems, not taking specific medications (melatonin, blood pressure, antidepressants, beta-blockers). Women taking oral contraception were allowed. Screened with Munich Chronotype Questionnaire (MCTQ) to ensure melatonin production between 23:00 and 01:00.
participants.recruitment: by e-mail, web posting, and word-of-mouth

stimuli_or_exposures.description: Participants viewed Apple iPads (iPad 1 or iPad 2, 9.7 inches diagonally, LED-backlit, 1024 × 728 pixels, full brightness, delivering 40 lux at the cornea) under three conditions: 1) Tablets-only, 2) Tablets viewed through clear-lens goggles equipped with blue light-emitting diodes (providing 40 lux of 470-nm light at the cornea), and 3) Tablets viewed through orange-tinted glasses (filtering out optical radiation below 525 nm ≈ 0). Two red lights (<1 lux) were present in the room in all conditions.

measures.construct: Personal light exposure (photopic illuminance, circadian light, circadian stimulus)
measures.instrument: Dimesimeter (records R, G, B sensors and activity levels)
Sleep logs, daily phone calls (for 7 subjects)

mechanisms: Short-wavelength light (peak sensitivity ≈ 460 nm) is maximally effective at suppressing melatonin.
The human circadian phototransduction model (Rea et al., 2005, 2010, 2011) predicts melatonin suppression based on spectral power distribution, duration of exposure, and pupil diameter.
moderators: Spectral power distribution of light (blue LEDs vs tablet-only vs orange-tinted glasses)
implementation_implications: Display manufacturers can tune the spectral power distribution of self-luminous devices to increase or decrease stimulation to the circadian system.
Software could be developed to control circadian light exposures based on the spectral power distribution of the display, time, and hours of operation to limit melatonin suppression in the evening.
Self-luminous electronic devices should be dimmed at night as much as possible to minimize melatonin suppression.
The duration of use of self-luminous devices should be limited prior to bedtimes.

limitations: The model of human circadian phototransduction (Rea et al., 2005) assumes a 1-h exposure, limiting predictions for 2-h exposures.

The current model only accounts for the absolute spectral power distribution of the light source; variables such as duration of exposure and spatial distribution need to be added to improve its predictive ability.
The type of task being performed on the tablets was not controlled, which could influence the amount of light delivered to the cornea.
Usage of self-luminous electronic devices before sleep may disrupt sleep even if melatonin is not suppressed, due to alerting or stressful stimuli from the tasks themselves.

mechanism_chain.description: Exposure to specific light levels and durations from self-luminous tablets, particularly blue light, stimulates retinal photoreceptors, which signal the circadian clock, leading to the inhibition of melatonin synthesis and subsequent suppression of melatonin levels.
